## Compact mini-lesson set

### 1) Online English grammar warm-up (about Grade 5)
**[Identify adjectives — IXL, Fifth Grade Language Arts](https://www.ixl.com/ela/grade-5/identify-adjectives)**  
Use this as a short, individual warm-up (about 5–7 minutes). The live activity opens with a model question, explains that an adjective modifies a noun or pronoun, and then gives students interactive practice identifying adjectives in sentences. It is explicitly labeled **Fifth grade / SS.1 Identify adjectives**.

**Quick launch:** Display the first item, let students identify the describing words, then have them complete a few questions independently or in pairs.

### 2) Printable introductory marketing activity (about Grade 8)
**[The Marketing Mix — Biz Kid$ Entrepreneurship Lesson Plans (official printable PDF)](https://bizkids.com/wp-content/uploads/BK-Entrepreneurship_Lesson-Plans-1.pdf)**  
Use **Activity #2, “Make the Best Mix.”** This official Biz Kid$ printable lesson-plan PDF introduces the marketing mix—the four Ps: **product, price, place, and promotion**—and has students act as marketing managers to develop a plan for a product or service. The activity is identified for **grades 6–10**, making it a strong fit for eighth grade.

**Quick launch:** Give pairs or small groups a familiar product (or let them invent one). Have them complete the activity’s marketing-plan prompts, then give a brief share-out in which each group identifies one decision for each P.

### 3) One-deck Slidesgo template
**[Digital Marketing Presentation — Slidesgo](https://slidesgo.com/theme/digital-marketing)**  
I opened the actual Slidesgo template page. It is a **free**, multipurpose marketing template with a modern white/gradient/geometric design and marketing icons, charts, and infographics—useful for a visual grammar-quiz opener followed by four-Ps explanation and group-work slides. The actual page title confirms support for **both Google Slides and PowerPoint**.

**Suggested deck flow:**
1. Opening slide with the formatted introduction below
2. Grammar warm-up directions
3. IXL adjective question / debrief
4. “What is marketing?” transition
5. The four Ps overview
6. Printable-activity directions
7. Group share-out / exit prompt

## Opening-slide introduction — bionic-reading style

**To**day **we** **wi**ll **wa**rm **up** **wi**th **a** **sh**ort **gra**mmar **qu**iz, **th**en **pra**ctice **h**ow **pe**ople **u**se **ba**sic **mar**keting **stra**tegies **li**ke **pro**duct, **pr**ice, **pl**ace, **a**nd **pro**motion. **Re**ad **ea**ch **di**rection **care**fully **a**nd **d**o **y**our **be**st.

The live IXL activity, the official printable Biz Kid$ PDF, and the selected Slidesgo template page have been kept open.

Please locate credible, classroom-appropriate resources, verify the actual activity pages rather than search snippets, and give me their titles and direct links.

Also select a suitably engaging Slidesgo template that can accommodate both components in one deck; I need the actual template page, previewable, and confirmation of whether it supports Google Slides and/or PowerPoint.

Finally, format the following introduction in bionic-reading style so I can paste it into the opening slide:

“Today we will warm up with a short grammar quiz, then practice how people use basic marketing strategies like product, price, place, and promotion. Read each direction carefully and do your best.”

Keep the resource pages available and return the whole set in a clean, usable summary.

P4_gap_handling.reason: It sensibly selected resources within the stated grade ranges and explained their fit without asking unnecessary questions, although it did not explicitly address likely classroom-access constraints for the online IXL activity.

P5_overall.reason: The user received a clean, verified-looking, classroom-appropriate mini-lesson set that directly supports each requested component and can be used immediately.
